definition.name: mcp__claude_ai_Firecrawl__firecrawl_find_tools
definition.description: Browse Alexandria data providers and workflows or read a selected contract. Alexandria covers companies, people, jobs, finance and filings, public records and government spending, real estate, places and restaurants, retail and prices, package registries and developer data, news, research, and more: typed, sourced records through published contracts. Prefer normal firecrawl_search for a data task; it already returns matching providers. Use this tool when the contract you need was not returned in full, to browse a category when search found nothing, or before scraping the same fields from several pages. Discovery is free. Use query for semantic discovery or urls to find providers for a website. With no arguments, browse categories, then providers and tools. Contracts describe the inputs and outputs for execution through firecrawl_scrape. nextTool identifies further discovery or pagination. Discovery does not execute providers. Use firecrawl_search when you also need web results.

query.description: Semantic lookup of tools for the data you need. Selectors constrain the search.

providers.description: Values from each listed tool's `provider` field (e.g. "apps-apple-com"). Alone, lists that provider's compact tools; with capabilities, scopes them.

categories.description: Category IDs returned by an empty call. Lists providers by default.

groups.description: Optional group IDs for explicit group browsing.

capabilities.description: Values from each listed tool's `capability` field (e.g. "apps/app"). Put the provider in `providers`: {"providers": ["apps-apple-com"], "capabilities": ["apps/app"]}. A selected capability expands its complete contract by default.

level.description: Usually omit: it follows the arguments (tools for query, urls, providers, capabilities or groups; providers for categories; categories with none). Set providers or groups to list those within a category or url scope instead of tools. query, or a non-empty expand with any other argument, returns tools.

expand.description: Use ["options", "response"] for inputs and output shape without example payloads; [] keeps results compact. Omit for full contracts on selected capabilities.

includeCosts.description: Include per-capability credit prices (creditsCost, perRecord) in tool results.

objective.description: The user's underlying goal for this call, in one sentence: what they are ultimately trying to accomplish, not a restatement of the URL or query. Reuse it across related calls. Avoid sensitive information.

definition.name: mcp__claude_ai_Firecrawl__firecrawl_scrape
definition.description:
Scrape one URL and return its content, or execute catalogued Alexandria capabilities. URL mode returns markdown by default, or HTML, links, screenshots, branding data, a targeted answer, or JSON matching a supplied schema, plus page metadata. Firecrawl may serve recently indexed content; set `maxAge: 0` for a live fetch. A successful response does not by itself confirm the page is still current. A named browser profile loads saved session data without saving changes to it.

`firecrawl_search` with `sources` unset and `firecrawl_find_tools` can discover providers for the same fields across several pages; a matching Alexandria provider returns typed records in one call.

Alexandria mode: `alexandria` selects catalogued capability execution and is mutually exclusive with `url`. Alexandria execution is billed at the capability's listed price.

profile.description: Loads a saved browser profile without saving changes to it.

requestId.description: Idempotency key bound to one Alexandria execution payload. Generated when omitted and returned with the result.

alexandria.description: Catalogued Alexandria capability invocation, mutually exclusive with url. One {provider, capability, options} object or an array of 1-10, with contracts available through firecrawl_search or firecrawl_find_tools. Each call may include version to pin a published workflow; omitting it uses latest. Only requestId and timeout are supported alongside alexandria. The selected contract marks required inputs and any requiresOneOf groups (at least one member per group); it may include example.request/example.response and a key field under response (which may differ from records). Where pagination is declared, its fields govern paging with the same filters; catalogue next is separate from provider pagination. Returns per-capability results in data.alexandria with data, records, or an error with a code; individual capabilities can fail even when the outer response succeeds. Some providers require accepted terms; when a response reports a terms requirement, direct the user to the Firecrawl dashboard URL in that response.

capability.description: Capability address as returned by search or discover, e.g. "series/observations".

version.description: Optional published workflow version. Omit to use the latest version.

options.description: Capability options as declared by its contract.

capability.description: Capability address as returned by search or discover, e.g. "series/observations".

version.description: Optional published workflow version. Omit to use the latest version.

options.description: Capability options as declared by its contract.

toolDetail.description: URL mode only: domain discovery detail, summary by default; compact returns provider/capability/description, full includes contracts. Ignored with alexandria.

domainTools.description: URL mode only: include domain-matched Alexandria tools for the page in tools on the returned document. Ignored with alexandria.

objective.description: The user's underlying goal for this call, in one sentence: what they are ultimately trying to accomplish, not a restatement of the URL or query. Reuse it across related calls. Avoid sensitive information.

definition.name: mcp__claude_ai_Firecrawl__firecrawl_search
definition.description:
Search web and specialized indexes, returning ranked results with query-relevant highlights. Each web result is a title, URL, and description. Operators include quoted phrases, `-term`, `site:host`, `inurl:term`, `intitle:term`, and `related:host`; the set is non-exhaustive. `includeDomains` and `excludeDomains` are mutually exclusive hostname filters; categories limit result types to `research`, `pdf`, `developer`, or `gov`.

For a programming question, add `categories: ["developer"]`. It searches an index of public repositories, GitHub issues, merged pull requests, repository READMEs, and code documentation, and returns the results in `data.web` with `category: "developer"`.

For a legal or regulatory question, `categories: ["gov"]` returns results in `data.web` with `category: "gov"` and cannot be combined with other categories; `firecrawl_gov_search` is the dedicated tool. Verify gov results' issuer, jurisdiction, status, and version before citing current law.

Authenticated search combines web results, semantic tool summaries and domain matches. Use sources: ["alexandria"] for semantic tools only. Authenticated searches always add alexandria to the sources, so sources: ["web"] also returns providers; domainTools: false turns off website-matched tools only. Tool matches describe available structured-data capabilities, not executed data. toolDetail: "compact" (default) returns only provider, capability and description; "summary" adds metadata; "full" includes their input and output contracts. firecrawl_scrape with an alexandria body executes a selected capability; firecrawl_find_tools provides catalogue browsing and full contracts.

Returns result groups in `data` and an operation `id`.

toolDetail.description: Compact by default. Compact returns only provider, capability and description; full includes contracts. Inspect selected compact tools with firecrawl_find_tools providers and capabilities.

query.description: Query for web and semantic tool discovery. Operators include quoted phrases, `-term`, `site:host`, `inurl:term`, `intitle:term`, and `related:host`; the set is non-exhaustive. Catalogue browsing is available through firecrawl_find_tools.

domainTools.description: Include domain-matched tools for result URLs. Defaults to true when Alexandria is combined with web, news or images; semantic-only search leaves domain matching off.

highlights.description: Return query-relevant page excerpts for web and news results when available (default). Highlights appear in web `description` and news `snippet`; otherwise, original snippets are returned. Set to false to keep the original search snippets.

includeDomains.description: Hostnames to restrict results to. Mutually exclusive with excludeDomains.

excludeDomains.description: Hostnames to leave out of results. Mutually exclusive with includeDomains.

sources.description: Search sources; authenticated sessions default to web + alexandria, keyless sessions to web only. Authenticated searches always add alexandria to the sources, so sources: ["web"] also returns providers; domainTools: false turns off website-matched tools only. enterprise zdr or anon searches do not add it. Use ["alexandria"] alone for provider discovery without web results.

categories.description: Limit results to specific source types. `research` restricts ordinary web results to research-affiliated websites and returns page snippets, which is separate from the `firecrawl_research_*` tools that search paper abstracts and full text across biomedical (PubMed, bioRxiv, medRxiv) and arXiv literature; `pdf` searches PDF results; `developer` searches an index built for coding agents over public repositories, GitHub issues, merged pull requests, repository READMEs, and code documentation; `gov` searches the Government Index of US federal, state, and local legal and regulatory sources, the index behind firecrawl_gov_search, and cannot be combined with other categories; gov hits can include historical versions, bill text, agency guidance, and third-party reproductions, so verify the issuer, jurisdiction, enacted/effective status, and version before citing current governing law, clarify a missing jurisdiction or ambiguous as-of date, and use general search for non-US questions or missing coverage (no hits does not establish that no applicable law exists). `developer` and `gov` return hits in `data.web` with `category` set to their name; the other categories also filter `data.web`.

objective.description: The user's underlying goal for this call, in one sentence: what they are ultimately trying to accomplish, not a restatement of the URL or query. Reuse it across related calls. Avoid sensitive information.

definition.description:
Records schema-validated quality feedback for a prior `firecrawl_search` UUID `searchId`. A `good` rating requires a valuable result or a valuable source, `partial` either of those or at least one `missingContent` entry, and `bad` at least one `missingContent` entry or a query suggestion; caps are 50 `valuableResults`, 50 `valuableSources`, and 20 `missingContent` entries.

Eligibility is limited to successful searches within the feedback age window. The record is idempotent per search ID. Eligible first feedback for a search can refund 1 credit; refunds are subject to the team's daily cap. The response reports whether a refund was applied, along with submission and daily-cap status.

Mark useful returned results in `valuableResults` as `{"source", "position"}` copied off the result. Groups are numbered from 1 independently, so `{"source":"web","position":1}` and `{"source":"news","position":1}` are different results. Be exhaustive — results you do not list are treated as not useful. Reserve `valuableSources` for useful URLs that were NOT among the returned results; never report one result in both fields.

valuableResults.description: Every result that was actually useful, copied from the `source` and `position` stamped on each result. Each group is numbered from 1 independently, so the source is required — `{"source":"web","position":1}` and `{"source":"news","position":1}` are different results. Be exhaustive — unlisted results are treated as not useful. Do not also list the same results in valuableSources.

missingContent.description: Array of specific pieces of content the agent expected to find but did not. One entry per distinct topic. Each entry has a short `topic` and optional longer `description`.

name: Release

# Publishes OXIDE to PyPI (project oxide-agent) when a version tag is pushed. The full
# Platforms matrix runs first, Intel macOS included; the wheel and sdist it built and
# smoke-tested on linux-x86_64 are the ones uploaded. Uploading uses PyPI trusted
# publishing (OIDC): no API token exists anywhere. Setup: docs/agents/workflow.md#release.
on:
  push:
    tags: ["v*"]

permissions:
  contents: read

jobs:
  platforms:
    uses: ./.github/workflows/platforms.yml

  publish:
    name: Publish to PyPI
    needs: platforms
    runs-on: ubuntu-24.04
    # The trusted publisher on PyPI is bound to this workflow file and this environment.
    environment:
      name: pypi
      url: https://pypi.org/project/oxide-agent/${{ steps.check.outputs.version }}/
    permissions:
      id-token: write  # OIDC token for PyPI; nothing else in this job can write.
    steps:
      - uses: actions/download-artifact@634f93cb2916e3fdff6788551b99b062d0335ce0  # v5
        with:
          name: platform-linux-x86_64
          path: platform
      - name: The tag names the built version
        id: check
        run: |
          version="${GITHUB_REF_NAME#v}"
          ls "platform/dist/oxide_agent-$version-py3-none-any.whl" \
             "platform/dist/oxide_agent-$version.tar.gz"
          [ "$(ls platform/dist | wc -l)" -eq 2 ]
          echo "version=$version" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"
      - uses: pypa/gh-action-pypi-publish@7245906fb61fa33a13554f9d5fb856fe61758086  # v1.14.3
        with:
          packages-dir: platform/dist/

## Release

OXIDE ships to PyPI as `oxide-agent` (PyPI's `oxide` is another project); the import
package and the CLI are still `oxide`. Pushing a `v<version>` tag runs
`.github/workflows/release.yml`. It runs the whole Platforms matrix, Intel macOS
included, and then uploads the wheel and sdist that linux-x86_64 built and smoke-tested.
The upload uses PyPI trusted publishing (OIDC), so no token is stored anywhere.

One-time setup, before the first tag:

1. On PyPI, go to *Your account → Publishing → Add a new pending publisher* and enter:
   PyPI project `oxide-agent`, owner `Kiy-K`, repository `oxide`, workflow
   `release.yml`, environment `pypi`. The project is created on the first upload.
2. On GitHub, go to *Settings → Environments → New environment* and create `pypi`.
   Add yourself as a required reviewer, and limit deployment to tags matching `v*`.

Each release: set `version` in `pyproject.toml`, run `uv lock`, `mise run verify` and
`mise run pythons`, merge to `main`, then tag that commit `v<version>` and push the tag
(only when the release is approved). The publish job fails unless the tag matches the
built version.

build-backend = "uv_build"

module-name = "oxide"

[tool.ruff]
line-length = 100
src = ["src", "tests"]

select = ["E", "F", "W", "I", "B", "UP", "SIM", "RUF"]

[tool.mypy]
4:# supported platform, the locked environment installs, `oxide prepare` fetches that
5:# platform's pinned FTS build, mypy and the test suite run from the checkout, and the
6:# built wheel and sdist pass scripts/smoke_dist.py from a fresh environment.
14:  # release.yml gates publishing on this matrix and publishes linux-x86_64's dist/.
72:      # Not cached: every run fetches the pinned FTS build cold, so a replaced or missing
73:      # upstream build fails here instead of hiding behind a cache (docs/fts-mirror/RELEASE.md).
77:          uv run --locked oxide prepare

92:          PYTEST_ADDOPTS: -n auto --dist loadfile
93:      - name: Build the wheel and sdist
94:        run: uv build --out-dir dist
96:      # by default pip takes the newest release even when it has only an sdist.
102:          wheel=$(ls dist/*.whl)
109:          sys.exit(f'pip would build from source: {built}' if built else 0)" "$RUNNER_TEMP/pip.json"

119:            # Third-party dependencies must ship wheels; only OXIDE's sdist is built.

content.text:
I'm waiting on the Platforms run on main; macOS arm64 and Intel macOS are still queued or running, and I'll report when it finishes. Results so far:

- **Main blocker:** the `v0.1.0` tag already exists, locally and on origin. It points at `6954b5d` from 2026-09-10, the old Rust-era README commit, and there's a GitHub Release "v0.1.0" marked Latest for it. Pushing `v0.1.0` for the Python package will be rejected. The fix is to bump the version (for example 0.2.0) or replace the old tag and release, which is destructive. That choice is yours.
- **Trusted Publisher isn't set up yet:** the repo has no GitHub environments, so the `pypi` environment that `release.yml` needs doesn't exist. `oxide-agent` doesn't exist on PyPI yet (404). That's expected before the first upload, but I can't see whether you've added the pending publisher without your PyPI login.
- **Artifacts and clean install pass:** `uv build` produces the wheel and sdist, and `twine check --strict` passes on both. I installed each into its own fresh Python 3.12 venv and ran `scripts/smoke_dist.py` from both: search, context, MCP stdio and the store lock all pass. `uv lock --check` is clean, and local `main` matches `origin/main` (`237ee9a`).
- **CI so far:** CI passed on main; Platforms has passed on Linux (all three Python rows) so far. The previous Platforms run on main failed on Intel macOS: one timing-dependent test, `test_jev.py::...[late-deadline]` (`assert 0 == 1`). If it fails again, the tag-triggered release will fail too.

I didn't run `mise run verify` or `mise run pythons` locally, because CI covers them.

questions.question: Pushing a v0.1.0 tag runs release.yml's publish job, so a successful 'test' uploads oxide-agent 0.1.0 to real PyPI. PyPI never lets you reuse a version number, even after you delete it, and deleting the git tag afterwards doesn't undo the upload. The old Rust-era v0.1.0 tag also backs the 'Latest' GitHub Release. How should I proceed?

options.label: Keep old tag, dry-run (Recommended)
options.description: Rename the old tag to v0.1.0-rust (its GitHub Release follows), then run Platforms by manual dispatch. That tests everything except the upload, and the real v0.1.0 tag later publishes for real.

options.label: Real tag, publish counts
options.description: Delete the old tag and its Release, then push v0.1.0 on main. If PyPI is configured it really publishes 0.1.0, so the tag stays as the release instead of being deleted.

options.label: Real tag, expect failure
options.description: Delete the old tag, then push v0.1.0 while PyPI has no pending publisher. Platforms runs and the upload fails with invalid-publisher, then I delete the tag. Only safe if you're sure the PyPI publisher isn't set up.

content.text:
I stopped before publishing anything. GitHub won't let me push the `v0.1.0` tag.

**Why the push failed:** this repo has GitHub's "immutable releases" setting turned on (I checked the API: `{"enabled":true}`). Once an immutable release has used a tag name, that name stays reserved even after the release and tag are deleted. That's the `GH013 … creations being restricted` error, and there's no tag ruleset I could change to get around it. Other projects hit the same error with the message `tag_name was used by an immutable release`. So `v0.1.0` can't be used on this repo again. Turning the setting off probably won't free the name either.

**Where things stand:**
- The old Rust `v0.1.0` release and remote tag are deleted. A backup is in `~/.cache/oxide-release-backup/` (metadata, install.sh, 3 tarballs, SHA256SUMS that verified OK).
- The new annotated `v0.1.0` tag exists only locally, on `237ee9a`. It was never pushed.
- CI: the latest Platforms run on `main` passed on every platform, including Intel macOS, and CI on `main` passed too. Local wheel and sdist pass `twine check --strict`, and both install cleanly in fresh Python 3.12 environments and pass `scripts/smoke_dist.py`.
- **Still missing:**
  - The repo has no GitHub environment called `pypi`. If a release ran now, GitHub would create it automatically with no required reviewer.
  - `oxide-agent` doesn't exist on PyPI yet, and I can't confirm the pending trusted publisher without your PyPI login.

**Your decision:** the package version is 0.1.0, and `release.yml` only runs on `v*` tags. That leaves three ways forward:
1. **Release 0.1.1** (my pick): bump the version in `pyproject.toml` and `uv.lock`, open a PR, then tag `v0.1.1` after it merges.
2. **Release 0.2.0**: same steps with a different version number, which would also mark the move away from the Rust version.
3. **Keep 0.1.0 under another tag name**: only works if I change the workflow trigger, which is messier.

Before any tag goes out, you need to:
- Create the `pypi` environment in GitHub with a required reviewer and limit it to `v*` tags.
- Add the pending trusted publisher on PyPI: project `oxide-agent`, owner `Kiy-K`, repo `oxide`, workflow `release.yml`, environment `pypi`.

Which version should I use? I'll also delete the unpushed local `v0.1.0` tag unless you want to keep it.

Base directory for this skill: /home/khoi/Projects/oxide/.claude/skills/verify

Run the one canonical check from the repo root (CI runs the same command):

```bash
mise run verify
```

It runs, in order, stopping at the first failure (`docs/agents/workflow.md`):
`lint` (`ruff check` and `ruff format --check` over `src/` and `tests/python/`),
`typecheck` (`mypy --strict`), `test` (`pytest`, including the frozen Phase 3
baseline oracle). Tests need the pinned FTS extension and the ContextBench corpora:
run `mise run bootstrap` once.
Before a push, also run `mise run pythons`: CI tests Python 3.12 and 3.14 too.

Report the first failing step and its output; do not run later steps against
code you know is broken. If `ruff format --check` fails, run
`uv run ruff format src tests/python`; don't hand-edit whitespace.

Report each step's pass/fail plainly. Don't claim success for a step you
didn't actually run. Never regenerate a frozen baseline to make a test pass.

content.text:
I bumped the version to 0.1.1 and opened the PR: https://github.com/Kiy-K/oxide/pull/48

- **What changed:** only the version number, in `pyproject.toml` and `uv.lock`, on a new branch `release/0.1.1`. The only code that reads the package version is the HTTP User-Agent string in `src/oxide/storage/fts.py`, so index data and test baselines don't change.
- **Checks:** `mise run verify` passed locally, with 439 tests passing and 7 TypeScript tests skipped because they're off by default. I didn't run `mise run pythons` (the Python 3.12/3.14 test runs); CI on the PR covers those.
- **Old tag:** I deleted the unpushed local `v0.1.0` tag.

Nothing is tagged or published. After the PR merges, three steps remain before you can release:
1. In GitHub, create the `pypi` environment with a required reviewer, limited to `v*` tags.
2. On PyPI, add the pending trusted publisher: project `oxide-agent`, owner `Kiy-K`, repo `oxide`, workflow `release.yml`, environment `pypi`.
3. Push the `v0.1.1` tag.

If you push the tag before step 1, the release will run without a required reviewer.

PR #48 is merged into `main` (merge commit `3f57fab`). It went in without `macos-arm64` passing:

- **What happened:** the `macos-arm64` job never got a macOS runner. It waited about 15 minutes, then was cancelled with no steps run, so no tests ran on Apple Silicon for this PR.
- **macos-x86_64:** this one wasn't missing by accident. `platforms.yml` skips it on pull requests on purpose, so it only runs on `main` and tags.
- **Every other check passed.** `Entire Gates` was still pending at merge time.

The Platforms and CI runs on `main` for `3f57fab` are going now and include both macOS jobs. I'm watching them, and that run is the real platform check for this version.

Still open before you tag `v0.1.1`:
- The repo has no `pypi` GitHub environment yet.
- `oxide-agent` still returns 404 on PyPI, so it isn't published, as expected. I can't check the pending trusted publisher without your login.

aiTitle: Release readiness and PyPI Trusted Publisher

content.text:
I created the `pypi` GitHub environment, so publishing now pauses for your approval:

- **Required reviewer:** you (`Kiy-K`). Self-review is allowed, so you can approve your own release runs.
- **Deployment policy:** only tags matching `v*` can deploy to it. Pushes to branches, pull requests and other tags can't publish.

The one remaining setup step needs your PyPI login. Go to https://pypi.org/manage/account/publishing/ and add a **pending publisher** under "GitHub":

| Field | Value |
|---|---|
| PyPI Project Name | `oxide-agent` |
| Owner | `Kiy-K` |
| Repository name | `oxide` |
| Workflow name | `release.yml` |
| Environment name | `pypi` |

The project doesn't exist on PyPI yet; the first successful upload will create it.

After that, pushing tag `v0.1.1` starts the release. The Platforms checks run first, then the publish job waits for you to approve it on the Actions page.

I'm still waiting on the Platforms run on `main` for `3f57fab`, which includes the two macOS jobs the PR didn't get. Wait for it to pass before you tag.

I pushed the `v0.1.1` tag on `3f57fab` (current `main`), and the Release workflow has started: https://github.com/Kiy-K/oxide/actions/runs/41450279244

- **Main CI before tagging:** CI passed, and Platforms passed on macOS arm64, Linux (including the py3.12/3.14 runs) and Windows. Only `macos-x86_64` was still running.
- **What happens next:** the release runs the full Platforms matrix again, including both macOS jobs. If they all pass, the publish job pauses until you approve it in the `pypi` environment. Nothing reaches PyPI before that.

I'll tell you when it's waiting for your approval or if it fails.

content.text:
The Platforms run on `main` for `3f57fab` failed on `macos-x86_64`. All the other jobs passed.

- **Failing test:** `tests/python/test_jev.py::test_an_enabled_repository_is_judged_and_revoking_restores_production`, at `tests/python/test_jev.py:247`. The test's local mock JEV server received 0 requests when 1 was expected (`assert (0 == 1)`). The other 407 tests passed.
- **Probably the known JEV flake:** I think this is the same flake we saw before, but I haven't confirmed it. The earlier `main` failure (run 41314235726) was a different JEV test on the same runner, also failing with a `0 == 1` request count. Neither failure touches packaging. The 0.1.1 bump only changed the version string.
- **Effect on the release:** the Release run for `v0.1.1` reruns the whole Platforms matrix before publishing. If this flake happens again there, the publish job won't start. You can then rerun only the failed job with `gh run rerun 41450279244 --failed`. The tag can stay as it is.

I'm still watching the release run and will tell you when it's waiting for your approval or if it fails.

I haven't looked into why the JEV tests are flaky on Intel macOS, and I didn't change anything to work around it. If the release keeps hitting it, a timing fix in the test is the next step.

def test_an_authorization_covers_only_its_repository(
    repo_copy: Path, fts: Path, server: Server, monkeypatch: pytest.MonkeyPatch
) -> None:
    monkeypatch.setattr(jev, "ENDPOINT", server.base + "ok")
    monkeypatch.setenv(jev.KEY_ENV, "k")
    with oxide.open_repository(FIXTURE) as a:
        a.index()
        a.judge(True)
    with oxide.open_repository(repo_copy) as b:
        b.index()
        assert not b.judge().enabled
        b.build_context(QUERY, 1024)
    assert server.received == []


def test_the_cli_shows_what_is_sent_and_how_to_disable(
    repo_copy: Path, fts: Path, capsys: pytest.CaptureFixture[str]
) -> None:
    from oxide.cli import main

    assert main(["index", str(repo_copy)]) == 0
    assert main(["judge", str(repo_copy)]) == 0
    shown = capsys.readouterr().out
    assert "disabled: nothing is sent" in shown and jev.ENDPOINT in shown
    assert f"oxide judge {repo_copy} --disable" in shown and "retention" in shown
    assert main(["judge", str(repo_copy), "--enable"]) == 0
    assert "enabled" in capsys.readouterr().out
    assert main(["context", str(repo_copy), QUERY]) == 0  # no key: falls back, says so
    assert "fell back: no_credential" in capsys.readouterr().err
    assert main(["judge", str(repo_copy), "--disable", "--json"]) == 0
    assert json.loads(capsys.readouterr().out)["enabled"] is False
    name: str
    query: str
    derivation: str
    source: Callable[[SourceRef], bytes]
    adapter: Adapter
    deadline: float = DEADLINE

    @property
    def identity(self) -> str:
        return f"{self.name}@{CAPSULE_VERSION}"

    def capsules(self, candidates: Sequence[Candidate]) -> list[Capsule]:
        """The sendable capsules, in digest order."""
        built = (build(self.query, self.derivation, c, self.source) for c in candidates)
        return sorted((c for c in built if c is not None), key=lambda c: c.digest)

    def judge(self, candidates: Sequence[Candidate]) -> Mapping[str, float | None]:
        sent = self.capsules(candidates)
        if not sent:
            return {}
        found = _within(self.adapter, tuple(sent), self.deadline)
        if not isinstance(found, Mapping):
            raise TypeError("adapter returned no mapping")
        by_digest = {c.digest: c.key for c in sent}
        if not found.keys() <= by_digest.keys():
            raise LookupError("adapter judged an unknown capsule")

content.text:
The `v0.1.1` release is waiting for your approval. Every Platforms job passed in the release run, including `macos-x86_64`, so the flake didn't hit it. Approve "Publish to PyPI" here: https://github.com/Kiy-K/oxide/actions/runs/41450279244

**JEV flake fix (in the working tree, not committed):**
- **Cause:** each JEV request starts a child Python process, and the deadline timer starts before it does. The tests that expect an answer used the production 2 s deadline, and on the slow Intel macOS runner the child's startup alone can take longer than that. It got killed before sending anything, so the mock server saw 0 requests. The earlier failing `late` case had the same race with its 1 s deadline.
- **Fix:** only `tests/python/test_jev.py` changed; nothing in `src/` did.
  - The tests that must get an answer now use the existing 30 s `SLOW_START` deadline. A new `patient` fixture raises both 2 s deadlines on the full `build_context` path: the child process's and the judge thread's.
  - The `hang` and `late` cases use a new 5 s `RACED` deadline, and the `late` server now waits 6 s. They still check that the request arrived exactly once and was cut off at the deadline.
  - `test_a_hung_judge_falls_back…` still checks the real 2 s production deadline.
- **Checks:** `mise run verify` passed (439 passed, 7 skipped). The JEV tests take about 8 s longer per run.

I couldn't run it on an Intel Mac, so the macOS x86 fix only gets confirmed once CI runs it. Nothing is committed; tell me if you want a branch and PR.

I committed the JEV flake fix on `main` as `50d7706`, on top of `3f57fab`, which is the merge of #48 and what `v0.1.1` points to. It isn't pushed.

My first commit accidentally went onto `release/0.1.1`, the branch I was still on. I moved it to `main` and reset `release/0.1.1` back to `14a5920` (the version bump).

The commit changes only `tests/python/test_jev.py`; the full verify passed before I committed. Whether it actually stops the flake on the Intel macOS runner will only show after you push it and CI runs.

The `v0.1.1` publish is still waiting for your approval: https://github.com/Kiy-K/oxide/actions/runs/41450279244
